correctness.rationale: For fixed integer \(k\) and \(n>2k\), the truncated geometric mean \(\mu_n(r)\) is continuous and strictly increasing because its derivative with respect to \(\log r\) is the positive variance. At \(r=k/(k+1)\), truncation strictly lowers the mean below \(k\), while the limit at \(r\uparrow1\) is \(n/2>k\), giving a unique integer-mean parameter. For fixed \(k\), that parameter converges to \(k/(k+1)\); the exact tail formula then converges to \((k/(k+1))^k\), and the latter tends to \(e^{-1}\). Reversal of the support preserves log-affinity and converts the tail into the event at or below the integer mean. Combined with the published lower bound, this proves the exact infimum. The checker only supplements the analytic proof.

value.rationale: The direct paper singles out the integer-mean case because it converts the Feige threshold into mass at or below the mean, compares it with stronger one-half bounds for classical families, and supplies a counterexample to one-half. Determining that the published \(e^{-1}\) lower bound is itself exactly sharp in this restricted subclass resolves the remaining quantitative gap with an explicit natural log-affine family. The result is structural rather than a finite numerical slice and clarifies that the arithmetic integrality constraint yields no universal improvement.
